claims.text: NbMoTaW is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy containing Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
A W-based refractory HEA incorporating Ta, Nb, and Mo can be an effective electrocatalyst for both HER and HOR.
The proposed HEA can provide greater catalytic activity and durability than conventional catalysts.
NbMoTaW can be synthesized from mixed elemental powders using selective laser melting.
The proposed W-based HEA exhibits a finely controlled multiphase microstructure containing lamellae or coherent particles.
Optimizing phase distribution and coherent boundaries modulates the alloy's electronic structure.
Engineered coherent boundaries provide resilience to catalyst deactivation.
Coherent lamellar interfaces and nanostructured features adjust the local d-band environment.
Electronic modifications induced by alloying lower the energy barrier for hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
Lower hydrogen adsorption and desorption barriers improve HER kinetics.
The robust HEA microstructure resists poisoning and structural degradation during electrochemical cycling.
Resistance to poisoning and structural degradation enhances durability in both HER and HOR.
The HEA should exhibit lower overpotentials than Pt-based catalysts or monometallic tungsten catalysts.
The HEA should exhibit more favorable Tafel slopes than Pt-based catalysts or monometallic tungsten catalysts.
The HEA should undergo less performance degradation during accelerated durability testing than Pt-based catalysts or monometallic tungsten catalysts.
State-of-the-art Pt catalysts provide the appropriate performance baseline.
The proposed performance enhancement is sensitive to alloy composition and microstructural tuning.
The anticipated benefits apply under moderate temperature and electrolyte conditions and may diminish under extreme conditions.
